main_text.l: teri Regimini & Jurisdictioni parebant.
Harum autem perpetua & Universa praxis
tot perspicuis & amplis in Scriptura Regulis
pariter & Exemplis confona, cum satis often-
datur in Epistolis ad Timotheum & Titum co
confilio scriptis, ad stabiliendum hoc maximè
Regimen, non in personis duntaxat Timothei
& Titi, sed in eorum etiam successoribus
(cùm Disciplina & Regimine haud magis
poflit Ecclesia quoad suum bene esse, quàm
verbo, & Sacramentis quoad Esse, destitui)
Miror illos, qui sic jus Episcopale & Au-
thoritatem maligne intuentur, ita penitus li-
vore occæcari, ut nec tantillum animadver-
tant, vel quis usus horum in Ecclesiâ, vel
quàm fit Ἀποστολικὴ [?] constitutio, quod utrum-
que in his Epistolis videtur haud minus per-
spicuè explicari, (tanquam scopus earum esset
& finis Principalis, ut peculiare quoddamMu-
nus, Jus & Authoritas instituatur & delege-
tur certis hominibus, qui Præsidentes Episcop-
i, cæteris in Ordinatione, Censuris, & reliquis
porrò Ecclesiasticæ Disciplinæ actibus praes-
ent) quam breviores illæ notæ Qualitatum
& Munerum ad Presbyteros, Episcopos, & Diaco-
nos pertinentium, alibi in eadem Epistola de-
scribuntur. In latiori enim sensu & promis-
cuo usu Nominis, utrofque horum mos erat,
(& fortasse nunc licet) appellare Episcopos,
quatenus Curam quandam ipsi, & Infpectio-
nem obtineant in Privatos suos Greges, quos

page.notes: Left margin: only damage and stains from the scan; no printed marginal text. Ἀποστολικὴ and Ἀποστολικοὶ: the first letter looks Greek on the scan and the rest is hard to read, so both are marked [?]. The word "teri" at the top is a fragment that continues from the previous page. The quoddamMu-nus join is as printed. Long s is written as a plain s throughout.
